ai_technology: Neural networks predict age and epigenetic lifestyle/health biomarker proxies from methylation principal components; a learned additive combination enables interpretable retrospective response analysis.

evidence.ai_role: Neural networks predict age and epigenetic lifestyle/health biomarker proxies from methylation principal components; a learned additive combination enables interpretable retrospective response analysis.
evidence.tested: Person-grouped nested cross-validation, replicate testing and retrospective analysis of existing intervention/control and external methylation datasets.
evidence.unknown: Lifestyle-weighted score is not a validated biological-aging or health-benefit endpoint; small external trial, tissue transfer and proxy interpretation limit inference.

organization: Tally Health; University of California, San Diego; TruDiagnostic

source_review.scope: Primary manuscript Methods, relevant Results, limitations and first-version publication metadata reviewed.

summary: CheekAI neural networks trained on 25,400 buccal methylation profiles from 14,716 adults were applied retrospectively to external datasets. In an existing eight-week randomized lifestyle trial with 18 intervention and 20 control participants, the model’s age-adjusted score decreased by 1.34 model-years relative to controls (p = 0.021), largely through dietary and metabolic proxy components. This preprint reports a learned methylation-score response, not demonstrated reversal of biological aging or improved health. The score was designed to reflect lifestyle proxies; a separate semaglutide analysis did not significantly reduce the overall score and showed tissue-transfer limitations.
title: Epigenetic deep learning detects a lifestyle-trial signature
